SPECIES

Ecological modelling for sustainable muskox management:

WP3 investigates how introduced muskoxen can be sustainably managed in a rapidly changing Arctic by combining population monitoring, ecological modelling, anthropology, and indigenous knowledge to co-produce practical conservation tools.

We plan on developing a flexible ecological modelling framework (i.e., spatially-explicit DEB-IBM) able to simulate and explore the cumulative impacts of changing environmental conditions or hunting regimes on individual muskox movement, behaviour and energy use, and their consequences on population trends.

Anthropological methods and insights will be employed to identify core concerns of hunters and other muskox stakeholders regarding muskoxen and their environments, and through a co-creation approach these concerns will be translated into real‑world inputs that can feed the model and help shape "what-if" scenarios that reflect Inuit practices and priorities.

One main output is to co-design a conservation toolkit, with hunters and wildlife managers, that can potentially support quota setting, habitat health, monitoring, and community livelihoods. The goal is to enable adaptive, culturally sensitive co‑management that balances ecological resilience with local needs in a rapidly changing Arctic.

While the model is primarily built with data from Zackenberg in NE Greenland, the anthropological fieldwork and collaboration with hunters and wildlife managers will focus on the muskox population around Kangerlussuaq in West Greenland.

Partners:

Astrid Oberborbeck Andersen, Aalborg University (anthropology: https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7811-1427)

Floris M. van Beest, Aarhus University (Arctic ecology: https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5701-4927)

Benjamin Dupuis, Aarhus University (Ecological Modelling: https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9633-8935)
